summary: Text Accumulator: collects stream fragments into growing text, and splits complete messages off a delimiter.
description: Each `add` appends the current `chunk` to a buffer. With an empty delimiter nothing is ever split and `accumulated` is simply the text so far — the mode a token stream wants. With a delimiter (newline by default) every complete piece moves to `messages` and only the unfinished tail stays in `accumulated`, so a message split across chunk boundaries reassembles correctly. Both stores are bounded: `maxLength` caps the pending buffer and `maxMessages` caps the retained list, dropping the oldest first and reporting the loss on `droppedCharacters` / `droppedMessages` plus an `overflowed` signal rather than growing without limit in a long-lived session. An empty chunk is ignored, so a stream's keep-alive frames do not fire `changed`.
whenToUse: Assembling anything that arrives in pieces: AI tokens into a displayable answer, log lines out of a chunked feed, NDJSON lines before parsing them. Pair it with Server-Sent Events or any node that emits fragments. Not needed when each event is already a whole value — wire that straight to its consumer.

ports.chunk: The fragment to append. Text, numbers and booleans are accepted; an object or an array is refused and named on `error`, because it means a JSON-parsed `data` output was wired here where the stream's `text` output was wanted.
ports.add: Appends the current chunk. Wire the stream's `onMessage` here; the chunk value arrives first.
ports.delimiter: Message boundary. Empty means no boundaries — accumulate everything, which is what a token stream needs.
ports.maxLength: Cap on the pending buffer in characters. Overflow drops the oldest and reports it; 0 disables the cap.
ports.maxMessages: Cap on retained complete messages. 0 keeps them all, which grows forever in a long session.
ports.accumulated: The text not yet terminated by a delimiter. With no delimiter this is the whole stream so far.
ports.lastMessage: The most recent complete message, for the common case of only wanting the newest.
ports.byteCount: UTF-8 size of the pending buffer, which differs from Character Count for anything non-ASCII.
ports.changed: Fires on every non-empty Add, so a Text node repaints as the stream arrives.
ports.messageReceived: Fires once per Add that completed at least one message — not once per message.
ports.overflowed: Fires when a cap dropped data. Wire it if losing the oldest content matters.
ports.error: Empty until something that is not text arrives on `chunk`, then a message naming what came and which output to wire instead. Clears on the next usable chunk and on Clear.

patterns: Server-Sent Events `text` → `chunk`, `onMessage` → `add`, delimiter empty, `accumulated` → Text `text`: an answer that types itself out.
Delimiter `\n` with `messages` → For Each renders a growing log without re-parsing the whole buffer each time.
The stream's `onOpen` → `clear` resets the accumulator when a new response starts.
antiPatterns: Wiring a stream's `data` output into `chunk`. `data` is JSON-parsed and is an object for an OpenAI-style payload; wire `text` (with the stream's `textPath` set) or a Function node that picks out the string field.
Leaving `maxMessages` at 0 in a session that runs for hours — the array grows until the tab does.
Wiring `add` from a signal that fires before `chunk` is set (a Function's own output, say) — the last chunk gets appended twice and the newest not at all.
